column2: A blank bar to build from scratch.
A bright spark at the edge of the fill.
A friendly focus wins over the tank. The focus is checked at the moment you press it, also in combat.
A group member to use as the tank. Empty uses the raid Main Tank, then the Dungeon Finder tank role. Updates out of combat.
A line at every 10% and a tick at every 5% across the bar.

A raid control panel with ready check, pull timer and target markers. In a raid it only shows while you are the leader or an assistant, since none of its buttons work without that; in a party it always shows.
Blizz Default also switches the reputation bar to Blizzard's.
Bright line on the swipe edge (needs a client with Cooldown:SetDrawEdge; native swipe only).
Clears your focus when you click the focus frame this way. Works in combat, where the right-click menu cannot clear focus.
Close Edit Mode first, then try again.
Compact Band puts markers, ready check and pull timer in one row you can resize in Unlock Mode. The other choices keep the window layouts.
Completed quest XP shows ahead of the fill in green, incomplete quest XP after it in gold. Quests under collapsed quest log headers are not counted.

Countdown length in seconds. Compact Band uses First with Ctrl + Left Click, Second with Shift + Left Click, Third with Left Click, and Right Click stops the timer. Set a timer to 0 to disable that shortcut.
Default for every icon on this bar; icons can override it.
Display junk items (grey quality and items you marked as junk) in a greyed-out style.
Empty = raid Main Tank, then tank role
Empty Slot: keeps this position free on the bar.
Equipped items get a rarity color border.
Flat paints the XP color. The gradients run from the XP color to the end color.
Full-width bar with the classic info blocks.
Full-window modes only. Shows start as a small icon, and the keybind switches between the icon and the full windows.
Full-window modes only. Which way the windows extend from the collapsed icon when they open.

Hide Until Usable: only shown while usable and off cooldown, such as Overpower or Victory Rush after a proc; low resources do not hide it. Hide Outside Form/Stance: only shown in the form or stance the spell needs, even on cooldown. Keep Place leaves the gap; the others close it.
Hides the Bloodlust and Heroism lockout debuffs.
Hovering a stat in the sidebar glows the equipped items that give it (Hit, Crit, Haste, Defense, Strength...).
Hunters and Rogues: an icon you click (or bind in Key Bindings > EllesmereUI Quality of Life) that casts Misdirection or Tricks of the Trade on your focus, else the tank, else a friendly target
Inspect Missing Enchant, Gem & Buckle Icons
Keeps the bar at max level, full, with the level and times. Time This Level shows total time played there.
Module Default follows the Raid Frames font outline from the Fonts page.
Native: the client's dark square sweep. Shaped: a drawn sweep that follows round icons and takes the Swipe Color.
Percent of the end caps' normal size.
Picks an NPC's only dialog option for you.
Positive values move both end caps away from the bar.
Pushes older messages along so a new one never overlaps them.
Raid Debuffs shows the common raid debuffs (armor, spell and physical damage taken, crit taken, attack power, attack and cast speed, healing taken, Judgements, Hunter's Mark) from anyone.
Reads the item's own stats; enchants and gems are not counted.
Return every EUI addon to its defaults.
Sell Junk skips items with no vendor price, equipment set gear and pinned items.

Shift + Left Click a marker icon to use its world marker item, then click the ground. Only markers whose item is in your bags get it; the rest keep Shift + Click to clear the target marker. Shift + Left Click the clear icon presses the server's Reset Markers button.
Show a small coin in the corner of items marked as junk.
Show Inspect Enchant Names Instead of Icons

Show the coin button in the bag header. Click it, then click items to mark or unmark them as junk. Junk goes into its own Junk category, and a Sell Junk button appears next to the coin while a merchant is open.
Shown at max level. Profession bonuses are only checked on your own sheet.
Shows the common raid debuffs from anyone: armor, spell and physical damage taken, crit taken, attack power, attack and cast speed, healing taken, Judgements and Hunter's Mark.
Shows the Convert to Raid button. In a raid of five or fewer it reads Convert to Party: everyone is removed and invited back to a new party.
Shows the debuffs you apply plus the common raid debuffs from anyone.
Shows the Disband button. It always asks before disbanding, but hiding it puts it out of misclick range for good.
Shows the hovered player's buffs as icons next to the tooltip (up to 16).
Shows the overlay, type icon and border colors only for debuffs you can currently dispel.
Shows the Reinvite button. It asks first, then removes everyone and invites them back to the same kind of group. Players have to accept the new invite.
Shows your damage taken, healing, avoids and combat enter/leave above the player frame instead of Blizzard's combat text, whose other messages are hidden while this is on. Move it in Unlock Mode.
The [Merfin] Experience Bar (Luxthos) WeakAura: blue to purple gradient, Quest XP Overlay, spark, rested after quest XP and seven texts with level, times and time to level.
The classic tooltip box around the meter window, with vanilla header buttons and every EllesmereUI meter feature.
The gap between a nested menu's icons and the entry that opens it.
The rested segment starts where the Quest XP Overlay ends instead of at your current XP.
The talent group this action menu works in. Outside it the keybind does nothing and the menu is hidden where it is nested.
This option requires an EllesmereUI Focus frame.
This option requires XP Bar Style EllesmereUI or Luxthos
Time This Session and XP per Hour carry on through a /reload (a load within five minutes) instead of starting over.

Toggles the Raid Tools panels, in or out of combat.

Left-click to set a keybind.
Right-click to unbind.
Use another action menu's keybind while that menu is not loaded. Both menus must be assigned to different specs.
Which buffs enemy nameplates show. Fine-tune it on the Aura Filters page.
Which ends of the bar show the gryphons.
